body:
This has probably been solved by a recent revert, if you are able to [build from source](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/engine_details/development/compiling/index.html) you can test latest `master`

Please test if this occurs in earlier 4.7 snapshots like rc1 and beta5 to see when this happened

Hmm, OK this is harder to test than I thought. When I restart the editor, it stops crashing. And then when I work on the game, it start happening again after a while. So, a few issues:

- Deleting uid_cache.bin might have not mattered at all, I restarted the editor when I did that so it made the bug disappear temporarily. Might not be related to uid at all.
- I can't tell if the issue is there with RC1 since it doesn't happen at first. (Guess I'll try working with RC1 for a bit)

So restarting the editor **temporarily** remove the crash, but it always come back. Some kind of leak maybe?

Can't quite say, but if it doesn't occur in RC1 there's a good chance it has been solved already, so I'd suggest either trying to build from source and test with latest `master`, or trying to see if it works with RC1, if you are unable to clearly define reproduction steps to test with

RC3 will probably be released later today with that fix in case you can't build from source

Wait to be clear I meant I don't know yet if it happens in RC1 or not, not that it doesn't happen.
(will update after editing with RC1 for a couple hours)

Good that's what I got from the comment, to clarify what I meant was to either:
* See if you can replicate it in RC1, if you can it's probably unrelated to the changes in RC2 that have been reverted
* See if you can replicate it building from source with latest `master`, or test with rc3 that should be out later today

Seems this is a relatively hard to trigger so it might not be highly critical as it doesn't seem to be happening to many others, at least not if it isn't from rc2 and it will have had some more time for people to test it

Thank you for doing further testing!

OK, it's crashing in RC1 now (I'll test RC3 too when it releases, but this already imply it might not be what you thought?)

I can also say it's "all or nothing": When I restart the editor it stops crashing, in every spot I mentioned before. But when it starts crashing again, it instantly happens in every trigger. So now that I've been working for 30 minutes with RC1 and that it switched to the "broken state" somehow: 
- If I click "Remote tree" in either my 2 heavy scenes : 100% crash
- If I click "Video Ram" in any scene (even empty) : 100% crash
- If I click my node with a dictionary of textures (in any scene, since it's an autoload) : 100% crash


I did another test with strange results: The crash when clicking "Remote tree" only happens in heavy scenes so I created a new scene to see if just the tree being large would trigger it:
>Node2D
>>CharacterBody2D (processing disabled, no child), duplicated x 714

(Total node count : 735, with my autoloads)

If I run this scene and click the remote tree, no issue, 0% crash.
Then, I add one more copy of the CharacterBody2D (node count 736) : 100% crash on clicking remote tree.
If I add more : 100% crash
If I delete some until the node count drop back to 735 : 0% crash

This isn't pure node count tho (maybe memory size?), because if I do the same with "Node2D" spam instead of "CharacterBody2D" then it starts crashing around 900 nodes rather than 735

Seems it is unrelated to that recent fix so probably not fixed by that

But would need some reproduction steps to clearly have some way to reproduce it

But to be clear: this is the same issue involving the UID cache? It seems strange that that would be causing that

Are you able to create a clean project with just the things required to trigger this and upload it as an MRP?

I think the UID cache didn't help in reality. At that time I just closed the editor -> deleted the cache -> opened the editor and noticed the bug was gone, so I figured it was a UID issue.
But now I know that simply _restarting the editor_ fix the bug temporarily, so it probably what happened: it's closing the editor that fixed the bug, not deleting the cache. Right know there's no proof that this is related to UID at all (but it's still the same issue. I just misdiagnosed before)

As for the MRP, this is pretty complicated because I don't know how to trigger the bugged state :/
Yesterday, I spent quite a while trying to make a MRP by copying parts of my projects to a clean one and seeing if it crash... but nothing worked. 
Problem is: the issue isn't there at first when opening the project, it only starts happening after <unknown trigger after working on my project for 30+ minutes>. So I can't tell if any MRP I make has the issue or not.

That makes it really hard to diagnose unfortunately

If you are able to replicate in your own project reliably one way to see would be to try to pinpoint when the bug started, by testing older pre-releases, that would allow us to pin down when or even specifically what change triggered the regression

I spent some time trying to create a MRP for this issue but I couldnt reproduce it on Godot 4.7 stable.

I tested the three reported debugger actions independently and together:

- opening and repeatedly refreshing the remote scene Tree
- selecting a remote node with a large exported dictionary of textures
- opening and repeatedly refreshing Debugger > Video ram


The stress project reached all of this without the game exiting or the debugger disconnecting:

- 30,000 runtime nodes in an isolated node-count test on Godot 4.7 stable;
- a combined stress test reaching 20,100 runtime nodes, 2,528 unique path-backed textures, and 35,808 texture dictionary entries;
- approximately 40–60 MiB reported in the Video RAM debugger during the stress tests;
- 427,008 path-backed resource churn operations on Godot 4.7 stable;
- retained-reference and pathless in-memory control runs without issue

I also tested the debugger's fixed 8 MiB TCP message boundary but well no issue there apart from:

`Condition "err != OK || size > out_buf.size() - 4" is true. Continuing.`

However well only that response is dropped, and the game continues, the debugger remains connected, and a subsequent small debugger response succeeds. So the outgoing 8 MiB limit does notreally explain the process termination

I also tested path-backed texture churn while repeatedly refreshing Video RAM I did:

- releasing replaced texture references;
- retaining all old references as a control;
- using pathless in-memory textures as a control;
- aggressive batches and repeated refreshes.

I did a diagnostic build on 4.8 that logged the suspected ResourceCache::has() / ResourceCache::get_ref() lifetime window and the debugger shutdown path, no cache-race warning, transport disconnect, request_quit, unexpected debugger-session stop, or editor-forced PID termination happened during these tests

The source code does explain why a debugger failure may look like the game closed normally: if the only debugger session is lost, the editor stops the active run and terminates its tracked child process. But well I couldn't really reproduce the failure or disconnect that would start this chain

Conclusion I arrived at is that raw node count, texture count, dictionary size, Video RAM response size, and uid_cache.bin alone are not sufficient to reproduce the issue ( though I didn't deliberately corrupt cache corpus but it doesnt seem related). The original problem may require another project-specific or transient condition, like a resource churn, malformed/imported resource state, a plugin or GDExtension, an inspector serialization edge case, or another long-session editor state.

The most useful evidence from an affected project would be:

- whether the project runs embedded or in a separate window
- enabled editor plugins and GDExtensions
- whether imported textures are being reimported/reloaded before the issue starts
- a Windows crash dump or exception code if the game faults first
- debugger transport/disconnect messages
- the exact last editor action before the session enters its consistently broken state


I honestly am defeated I can't really figure out what is wrong, if you can provide any of the above when I have time I will look into it further, or just generally anything more. Thank you.
